claim: The hub reaches the ports on a plane side. Glue a knot space along a simple 3-edge cut, remove a near line M, and suppose the interface has six patterns. (1) Tie class (proved): on a plane near side with Kasteleyn signs the hub's tie class contains every point on M's three faces. The solutions are perfect matchings of lines to faces, two of which differ by alternating cycles that flip exactly the points they enclose and never enter M's faces (325 removals on 30 plane spaces; equal at 321). (2) Route lemma (proved, any near side): suppose the hub and a near point a pin the closing pattern to t, and either (i) the hub is tied to a port other than t's odd port, or (ii) the hub and t's two other ports form a near knot whose excluded pattern, at the pinning hub value, differs from t in one of those ports. Then every three-point crossing knot {h, a, c} with c separating t is generated, whatever the far side, because the far knot through the two non-odd ports is automatic. (3) Access lemma (checked): on the 30 plane spaces all 4560 pinnings are of type (i) or (ii); on the Fano plane and census 58 all 336 are of neither type. (4) Hence on these 30 plane near sides no pinned-and-separated three-point knot is new at a six-pattern removal, for any far side; the routes are confirmed knot by knot (2142 knots). (5) Every new knot found (1884 more, from the two non-planar near sides glued to census and 10-point plane far sides) is a pinned-and-separated three-point knot through the hub. Open: the access lemma for every plane space, that every new knot has this form, and the four-pattern removals (no creation found).
